title: Trump Wants to Roll Back Fuel Rules — What Does That Mean for Cars?
summary:
Have you ever wondered why some cars use less gas than others? The government has rules about that. And now President Donald Trump wants to change them.

On Saturday, Trump announced new fuel economy standards that roll back rules put in place by former President Joe Biden. Trump said the old rules were like an "EV mandate" — a requirement that pushed people to buy electric vehicles. He wrote on social media that the new standards would "take the waste out of building cars in America" and mean "LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car."

But here's a fact check: there is no federal law that requires Americans to buy electric cars or bans gasoline cars. The real rules are called Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards. They were created by Congress in 1975 and require carmakers to meet average fuel economy targets across all the cars and light trucks they sell. Under Biden, the rules were set to rise from 39.1 miles per gallon to about 50.4 mpg by 2031.

Trump hasn't said exactly what the new numbers will be. But in December 2025, he proposed a fleetwide average of about 34.5 mpg by 2031 — more than 30 percent lower than Biden's rule. The Transportation Secretary said an announcement is "COMING MONDAY."
why_it_matters: Fuel rules decide how much money families spend on gas and how much pollution goes into the air, so a decision made in Washington can reach your family's driveway — and your future.

background_read: The first fuel economy rules were made in the 1970s, after an oil crisis caused gasoline prices to jump and drivers waited in long lines at gas stations. Congress wanted cars to use less gas so the country would not depend so much on oil.

Joe Biden (the U.S. president from 2021 to 2025) made the standards stricter, while Donald Trump (president again since 2025) says rules like that push people toward electric cars and make new cars cost more.

Electric vehicles (cars that run on batteries instead of gasoline) are getting more common, but most new cars sold in the United States still run on gasoline, so these rules affect almost every family that buys a car. The Transportation Secretary (the person in charge of the U.S. department that handles roads, cars, and planes) said a bigger announcement is coming soon.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, former President Joe Biden, Congress, and U.S. carmakers
WHAT: Trump announced new fuel economy standards that roll back Biden-era rules; he called the old rules an "EV mandate" but has not said the exact new numbers
WHERE: The United States — announced on social media, with the Transportation Secretary promising an announcement "COMING MONDAY"
WHY: These rules decide how much gas cars must save, which affects the prices families pay and the kinds of cars companies build

perspectives.description: They say the old rules pushed people toward electric cars and made new vehicles more expensive, and that weaker rules mean lower prices and more choices for families.
They warn that weaker standards mean cars burn more gasoline, which creates more pollution and makes it harder to fight climate change.
Car companies must plan new models years ahead, so rules that change every time a new president takes office make it hard to decide what to build.
